name: Pin and trust images
objective: CKS › Supply Chain Security (20%). Drill EVERY supply-chain corner harder than the exam: Trivy CVE scanning with severity gates, static manifest analysis with kubesec, digest pinning, banning :latest, ImagePullPolicy hardening, an approved-registry ValidatingAdmissionPolicy + binding, a VAP that bans :latest, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a broken binding. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Pin an image by digest (@sha256:)
questions.teach:
A tag like `:1.36` is **mutable** — the registry owner can repoint it. A **digest** (`@sha256:<64 hex>`) is the hash of the exact image content, so it is **immutable**: the kubelet pulls precisely those bytes or fails. Pin with `image: busybox@sha256:<64 hex>`.

**Gotcha:** a digest is per-architecture — one copied from another arch won't pull on your node.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`, create a pod `digest-pod` (container `app`, command `sleep 3600`) whose image is pinned **by digest** — `busybox@sha256:<64-hex-digest>` (any valid busybox digest).

Target: pod `digest-pod` exists; its container image is `busybox@sha256:` followed by a 64-char hex digest (not a plain tag).
questions.hint: Find a digest with `crane digest busybox:1.36` or `docker buildx imagetools inspect busybox:1.36`, or reuse a known one. Set `image: busybox@sha256:<64-hex>`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: digest-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox@sha256:9ae97d36d26566ff84e8893c64a6dc4fe8ca6d1144bf5b87b2b85a32def253c7
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML
questions.eli5:
Think about ordering a specific book. A **tag** like `busybox:1.36` is like asking for "the latest printing of this title." Sounds precise — but the publisher can quietly swap what rolls off the press under that name. Next time you order "1.36," you might get a *different* book with the same cover.

A **digest** (`busybox@sha256:<64 hex characters>`) is like ordering a book by its exact fingerprint — a hash computed from every byte of its content. If even one word changed, the fingerprint changes. So a digest always gets you *exactly* those bytes, or nothing at all. That's what "immutable" means: nobody can repoint it behind your back.

In Kubernetes you pin by putting the digest in the `image:` field instead of a tag. The kubelet pulls precisely that content and verifies the hash.

**But watch out:**

- A digest is **per-architecture**. The fingerprint for the amd64 build is different from the arm64 one. Copy a digest from the wrong CPU type and the pull **fails** on your node.
- A digest is **long and unforgiving** — it must be `@sha256:` followed by **exactly 64 hex characters**. A truncated or mistyped digest won't pull.
- Digests are **unreadable to humans** — you can't tell `9ae97d...` is "version 1.36." Teams often pin *both* (`busybox:1.36@sha256:...`) so people can read the tag while the digest does the real locking.
- Pinning by digest locks the **content**, but it does **not** verify *who* published it — that's image **signing** (a separate concept).
questions.deepDive:
## Pinning images by digest — full rundown

### Mental model
An image reference has the shape `registry/repository:tag@sha256:<digest>`. A **tag** is a human-friendly, **mutable** pointer — the registry owner can repoint `:1.36` to new content at any time. A **digest** is the **content hash** of the exact image manifest: `@sha256:` followed by 64 hex characters. It is **immutable** — the kubelet pulls precisely those bytes and verifies the hash, or the pull fails. Digest pinning is the supply-chain control that guarantees "what I tested is exactly what runs."

### Reference anatomy
| Form | Example | Mutable? |
|---|---|---|
| tag | `busybox:1.36` | ✅ owner can repoint |
| untagged | `busybox` | ✅ resolves to `:latest` |
| digest | `busybox@sha256:9ae9…53c7` | ❌ immutable, content-addressed |
| tag + digest | `busybox:1.36@sha256:9ae9…53c7` | ❌ digest wins; tag is documentation |

### Pinning in a pod
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: digest-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox@sha256:9ae97d36d26566ff84e8893c64a6dc4fe8ca6d1144bf5b87b2b85a32def253c7
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
```

### Finding a digest
```bash
# crane (go-containerregistry) — returns the manifest digest
crane digest busybox:1.36

# docker buildx — inspect the manifest/index
docker buildx imagetools inspect busybox:1.36

# docker (after a pull) — RepoDigests field
docker inspect busybox:1.36 --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'

# skopeo — remote inspect without pulling
skopeo inspect docker://busybox:1.36 | grep -i digest
```

### Multi-arch caveat
A tag like `busybox:1.36` usually points at a **manifest list (image index)** that contains one child manifest per architecture, each with its **own digest**. The digest from `crane digest busybox:1.36` is the *index* digest (arch-independent — the kubelet picks the right child). A **per-arch child digest** only pulls on that architecture:

| Digest kind | Pulls on |
|---|---|
| index/manifest-list digest | any supported arch (kubelet selects child) |
| amd64 child digest | amd64 nodes only |
| arm64 child digest | arm64 nodes only |

Pinning an arch-specific child digest on the wrong node gives `no matching manifest for <platform>`.

### Why digests > tags for supply chain
- **Reproducibility** — the same manifest every deploy; "works on my cluster" becomes deterministic.
- **Tamper resistance** — a repointed/poisoned tag cannot silently reach you; the hash wouldn't match.
- **Audit** — the running content is provably the content you scanned.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Digest must be `@sha256:` + exactly 64 lowercase hex chars.** Truncated/typo'd digests fail to pull with `invalid reference format` or `manifest unknown`.
- **Per-architecture:** an arch-specific child digest won't pull on a different arch. Prefer the index digest, or match the node's arch.
- A digest locks **content, not provenance** — it does not prove *who* built it. Authenticity requires **cosign** signing/verification (separate lesson).
- When both a tag and a digest are present (`repo:tag@sha256:…`), the **digest is authoritative**; the tag is ignored for the pull and serves only as a label.
- `imagePullPolicy` is largely moot for a digest ref — content is already uniquely identified, so there is nothing to "re-pull and swap."

### Quick reference
```bash
crane digest busybox:1.36                 # -> sha256:....
# pin it:
#   image: busybox@sha256:<64-hex>
kubectl get pod digest-pod -n cks-supply \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}'   # verify @sha256:<64-hex>
```

questions.title: Ban :latest — pin a real version + imagePullPolicy
questions.teach:
`:latest` floats to whatever was pushed last, so two deploys of the "same" image can run different code. Pin an explicit tag or digest, and set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` so a pinned tag isn't silently re-pulled and swapped.

**Gotcha:** an **untagged** image (`nginx`) silently resolves to `nginx:latest` — just as bad as writing `:latest`.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`, create a **Deployment** named `web` (1 replica, container `web`) whose image is a **pinned version** — NOT `:latest`, NOT untagged. Use `nginx:1.25-alpine`, and set `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` on the container.

Target: Deployment `web` exists; its container is named `web`, image carries an explicit tag (not `:latest`, not untagged) or `@sha256:`, and `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create deployment web -n cks-supply --image=nginx:1.25-alpine` names the container `nginx`, not `web` — build YAML so the container is named `web`. Add `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: web } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: web } }
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:1.25-alpine
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
YAML

verification.description: Deployment web: container 'web', pinned image (not :latest), imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent

questions.eli5:
`:latest` sounds great — "give me the newest!" — but it's a trap. Imagine a milk carton labelled just **"MILK"** with no date. Today's carton and next week's both say "MILK," but they're different milk. If you deploy twice using `:latest`, you can get two *different* builds of code while swearing they're "the same image." When something breaks, you can't even tell which version is running.

The fix is to **pin a real version** — `nginx:1.25-alpine` — so "the same image" truly means the same code every time.

The second half is **`imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`**. This tells the kubelet: *"if you already have this image cached on the node, use it — don't phone the registry again."* That stops a surprise re-pull from silently swapping the bytes under you, and it's faster.

**But watch out:**

- An **untagged** image is a silent `:latest`! Writing `nginx` secretly means `nginx:latest` — just as bad. Always write an explicit tag.
- **`imagePullPolicy` defaults are sneaky.** If you use the `:latest` tag (or no tag), the default policy becomes **`Always`** — it re-pulls every start. For any other tag the default is `IfNotPresent`. Another reason to avoid `:latest`.
- `IfNotPresent` **trusts the node's cache**. If a node already cached a stale "1.25-alpine," it keeps it. A **digest** is the truly bulletproof pin; a tag + `IfNotPresent` is good but not immutable.
- Pinning a tag protects you from *drift*, but a tag can still be *repointed* by the registry owner — a **digest** closes that last gap.
questions.deepDive:
## Banning `:latest` + imagePullPolicy hardening — full rundown

### Mental model
`:latest` is a **floating** tag: it points at whatever was pushed most recently, so two deploys of "the same" image can run different code. Supply-chain hygiene means every workload names an **explicit, immutable-ish reference** (a pinned tag, ideally a digest) and uses an **`imagePullPolicy`** that doesn't silently re-pull and swap bytes. This lesson pins a real version and sets `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`.

### The reference problem
| Image field | Resolves to | Safe? |
|---|---|---|
| `nginx:latest` | floating latest push | ❌ non-reproducible |
| `nginx` | **`nginx:latest`** (implicit) | ❌ same problem, hidden |
| `nginx:1.25-alpine` | fixed tag | ✅ pinned (but tag can be repointed) |
| `nginx@sha256:…` | content hash | ✅✅ immutable |

Writing an **untagged** image is the classic trap: it is exactly `:latest`.

### imagePullPolicy — the three values
| Policy | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Always` | contact registry every pod start; pull if digest differs |
| `IfNotPresent` | use the node's cached image if present; pull only if missing |
| `Never` | only use a pre-present image; never pull (fails if absent) |

### The sneaky defaults
If you **omit** `imagePullPolicy`, Kubernetes infers it from the tag:

| Image ref | Defaulted policy |
|---|---|
| tag `:latest` | **`Always`** |
| **untagged** (implicit `:latest`) | **`Always`** |
| any other explicit tag (`:1.25-alpine`) | `IfNotPresent` |
| digest `@sha256:…` | `IfNotPresent` |

So `:latest` is doubly bad: non-reproducible content *and* an implicit `Always` re-pull. Pinning a real tag and **explicitly** setting `IfNotPresent` removes both surprises.

### The Deployment
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: web } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: web } }
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web                 # container name must be "web"
        image: nginx:1.25-alpine  # pinned, not :latest, not untagged
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

### Why `kubectl create deployment` isn't enough here
```bash
kubectl create deployment web -n cks-supply --image=nginx:1.25-alpine
```
This names the **container** after the image (`nginx`), not `web`, and sets no explicit `imagePullPolicy`. When the target requires a container named `web` with `IfNotPresent`, author the YAML (or `kubectl create ... --dry-run=client -o yaml` then edit).

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Untagged == `:latest`.** `image: nginx` fails a "no :latest" rule just like `nginx:latest`.
- **Omitting `imagePullPolicy` with `:latest` gives `Always`** — re-pulls every start, inviting a silent swap. Set it explicitly.
- `IfNotPresent` **trusts the node cache** — a tag can still have been repointed and cached. For true immutability pin a **digest** (`@sha256:…`).
- `kubectl create deployment` names the container after the image; when the grader checks the container name, build YAML instead.
- `Never` fails outright if the image isn't already on the node — only use it for pre-loaded images (e.g. kind-loaded).
- A pinned **tag** still relies on the owner not repointing it; a **digest** is the only reference that is cryptographically fixed.

### Quick reference
```bash
# generate and edit
kubectl create deployment web -n cks-supply --image=nginx:1.25-alpine \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml > web.yaml
#   -> set container name to web, add imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
kubectl apply -f web.yaml

kubectl get deploy web -n cks-supply \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].name}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}{" "}{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].imagePullPolicy}{"\n"}'
```

questions.title: Private-registry pull via imagePullSecrets
questions.teach:
Images from a private registry need credentials: create a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret with `kubectl create secret docker-registry`, then reference it under the pod spec's `imagePullSecrets`. The kubelet uses it to authenticate the pull.

**Gotcha:** `imagePullSecrets` lives on the **pod spec** (`spec.imagePullSecrets`), not on the container — and the Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-supply`: (1) create a docker-registry Secret `regcred` for server `registry.internal:5000`, username `ci`, password `s3cr3t`; (2) create pod `private-pod` (image `busybox:1.36`, container `app`, `sleep 3600`) that references `regcred` under `spec.imagePullSecrets`.

Target: Secret `regcred` is type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`; pod `private-pod` lists `regcred` in `spec.imagePullSecrets`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t`. Then in the pod spec add `imagePullSecrets: [ { name: regcred } ]`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: private-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  imagePullSecrets:
  - name: regcred
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

verification.description: regcred dockerconfigjson Secret + private-pod referencing it in imagePullSecrets

questions.eli5:
Public images are like books on a free library shelf — anyone can grab them. A **private registry** is more like a members-only storeroom: before the kubelet can pull an image out, it has to show a membership card at the door.

That membership card is a special Secret of type **`dockerconfigjson`**. You create it with one command, handing over the registry address, your username, and your password:

```
kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t
```

Kubernetes packs those into the exact file format a Docker client uses to log in. Then you tell the pod *"use this card at the door"* by listing the Secret under **`imagePullSecrets`**. When the kubelet pulls the image, it presents the credentials and gets let in.

**But watch out:**

- **`imagePullSecrets` goes on the POD spec, not the container.** It sits at `spec.imagePullSecrets`, alongside `containers:` — a very common mix-up. It's a login for *pulling*, so it belongs to the whole pod, not one container.
- The Secret must live in the **same namespace** as the pod. A pull secret in `default` can't help a pod in `cks-supply`.
- It must be the right **type: `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`**. A plain generic Secret won't work, even with the right keys.
- The value is the **field `name:`** — `imagePullSecrets: [{ name: regcred }]`, a list of name references, not the Secret's contents.
- The `--docker-server` must match the registry host in your `image:` exactly, or the kubelet won't apply the right credentials.
questions.deepDive:
## Private-registry pulls with imagePullSecrets — full rundown

### Mental model
To pull from a registry that requires authentication, the kubelet needs credentials. You store those credentials in a Secret of type **`kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`** (the same format as `~/.docker/config.json`), then attach it to the pod via **`spec.imagePullSecrets`**. At pull time the kubelet decodes the Secret and authenticates to the matching registry.

### Creating the Secret
```bash
kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 \
  --docker-username=ci \
  --docker-password=s3cr3t \
  --docker-email=ci@example.com      # optional
```
This produces a Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` whose single key is `.dockerconfigjson`:
```json
{ "auths": { "registry.internal:5000": {
    "username": "ci", "password": "s3cr3t",
    "auth": "<base64(ci:s3cr3t)>" } } }
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--docker-server` | registry host[:port] — **must match the image's registry** |
| `--docker-username` | registry user |
| `--docker-password` | registry password / token |
| `--docker-email` | optional, legacy |

### Referencing it from the pod
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: private-pod
  namespace: cks-supply
spec:
  imagePullSecrets:          # POD spec, sibling of containers
  - name: regcred            # a NAME reference, not the contents
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
```
`imagePullSecrets` is a **list of local object references** (`{ name: <secret> }`), resolved in the pod's own namespace.

### Where it lives — pod vs container vs ServiceAccount
| Location | Valid? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `spec.imagePullSecrets` | ✅ | the pod-level field |
| `spec.containers[].imagePullSecrets` | ❌ | no such field |
| ServiceAccount `imagePullSecrets` | ✅ | auto-injected into pods using that SA |

Attaching to a **ServiceAccount** is the scalable pattern — every pod using that SA inherits the pull secret without per-pod config:
```bash
kubectl -n cks-supply patch serviceaccount default \
  -p '{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"regcred"}]}'
```

### How the kubelet matches credentials
The kubelet picks the entry under `auths` whose host matches the **registry portion** of the image reference. If `--docker-server` doesn't match the image's registry host exactly (including port), the credential isn't applied and the pull fails with `ImagePullBackOff` / `401 Unauthorized`.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`imagePullSecrets` is on the pod spec, not the container.** Putting it under `containers[]` is invalid — a frequent exam mistake.
- **Secret and pod must share a namespace.** `imagePullSecrets` resolves only within the pod's namespace.
- **Type must be `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.** A generic Secret with the right data won't be treated as a pull secret. Always use `create secret docker-registry` (or set `type` explicitly).
- **It's a name reference** — `- name: regcred`, not the Secret's data inline.
- **`--docker-server` must match the image host** exactly (host + port). Mismatch → auth not applied → `ErrImagePull`.
- Debugging: `kubectl describe pod` shows `Failed to pull image … 401 Unauthorized` when the secret is missing/wrong.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n cks-supply create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=registry.internal:5000 --docker-username=ci --docker-password=s3cr3t

kubectl -n cks-supply get secret regcred -o jsonpath='{.type}{"\n"}'  # kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson

# pod references it under spec.imagePullSecrets:
#   spec:
#     imagePullSecrets:
#     - name: regcred
```
